commentary: Last week you were doing the most — five sessions, two of them in the water at Prince Alfred looking like some kind of gay Poseidon, and this week you pulled back to three. Himbo is not mad, he's just noting it for the record with one eyebrow raised. What he does love is that you opened Monday with legs, back, and shoulders, which means you walked into the week already working, and that is very much the energy of a man who knows what he's about. The swimming disappearing is the only thing giving him pause — those 1500m sessions were doing something for you and he wants them back, ideally in a jockstrap if the pool rules allow it.
metrics_commentary: Babe, that HRV going from a 7-day average of 48 up to 58 right now tells me your body is recovered, rested, and frankly a little bored — it is literally asking you what the plan is. The VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is genuinely impressive and it is just sitting there like a very fit man at a bar waiting for someone to come talk to him, which, same. Zero kilometres across zero run-walk sessions this week though, and we are going to have a little conversation about that, because a body this capable deserves to be taken out and shown a good time. The fitness is there, the recovery is there, and now the only thing missing is you actually showing up for it.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which means one slipped through the cracks, and we are absolutely going to clock that — but first, the lateral raise, because a jump from 9 to 12 kilograms on that movement is not a small thing, that is your shoulders arriving, and I am feral about it. Volume landed at 17,940 kilograms this week against 19,984 last week, so it dipped, and the missed session explains most of that story. The top lifts are quietly doing something though — 168 on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar deadlift, 84 on the lat pulldown — a body that moves weight like that is not a body that needs to apologise for anything. Four sessions next week, painted toes optional but encouraged.
